page: OVHcloud l40s-180 is a GPU-accelerated server powered by an AMD EPYC 9124 processor with 30 dedicated physical cores operating at 2.75 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The hardware configuration includes 180 GB of system memory, providing 6.0 GB per core. For acceleration, the server features two NVIDIA L40S GPUs based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, delivering a combined 96 GB of VRAM. Local storage is provided by a 400 GB NVMe SSD, and network connectivity is supported by a 16 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Benchmark results indicate strong compute and memory performance. The dedicated AMD EPYC processor achieves top 25% scores in stress-ng single-core and multi-core evaluations, as well as in Passmark CPU tests, including extended instructions, encryption, and physics. Memory bandwidth for small cached blocks is also in the top 25%. Most notably, the dual NVIDIA L40S GPUs deliver top-tier performance in large language model inference tasks, spanning prompt processing and text generation across 135M, 7B, and 70B model sizes.

From a resource density perspective, the server offers a highly specialized hardware profile, balancing dedicated x86_64 compute cores with high-capacity GPU accelerators. This makes the instance highly cost-efficient for workloads that require parallel processing power without the overhead of larger, multi-GPU clusters. The server is optimized for workloads such as LLM inference, machine learning model training, data science pipelines, high-performance computing, and database operations, supported by its strong Redis SET and database benchmark performance.
description: The OVHcloud l40s-180 is a dedicated GPU-accelerated server designed for compute-intensive and artificial intelligence workloads. It features an AMD EPYC 9124 processor with 30 dedicated physical cores running at 2.75 GHz, paired with 180 GB of system memory. Acceleration is driven by two NVIDIA L40S GPUs from the Ada Lovelace architecture, providing a total of 96 GB of VRAM. Storage and networking are supported by a 400 GB NVMe SSD and a 16 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark data highlights top-tier performance in LLM inference across small, medium, and large models, alongside strong CPU compute, encryption, and database capabilities. This configuration is highly suited for machine learning inference, data science, and high-performance database operations.
